The new note is appended to `warning` on the same code path that calls `_roborev_reviewer(...)` at line 836, i.e. when a real reviewer gate is being run. At that moment `it.gates[gate]` is still the *previous* record, so `untriaged_note` reads the previous round's `chunk_findings` and emits `"NOTE: <gate> has untriaged finding(s) #N from its last review; they stay on the record ..."`. So the recording that follows the warning replaces the very findings the warning promised would "stay on the record", and the numbers it printed no longer address the same findings.

Concrete repro: (1) `ddflow review <id> critic` leaves finding #1 untriaged; (2) run the gate again (`ddflow review <id> critic`, or any reviewer-gate run). chunk_findings.detail: The warning this fix promises for a manual gate record is wired into the wrong path. `untriaged_note` is only reached from the measured-review API shown here — the function that calls `_roborev_reviewer(...)` (which consults the roborev attribution) and then `R.record_measured(...)`, i.e. the `ddflow review` recording path. The path the bug is actually about (`ddflow gate record <id> critic --outcome passed`, the hand record whose untriaged findings were being orphaned) is applied by the event handler in `ddflow/core/handlers/gates.py`, and that handler neither calls `untriaged_note` nor produces any operator-visible output. Concrete repro: with an untriaged finding left by the previous round, run `ddflow gate record <id> critic --outcome passed` and observe that no note listing `#1`/`#2` is printed, so the operator is never told the findings remain untriaged — exactly the "silently orphan them" complaint the intent says must be fixed. Conversely, in the path where the note *is* printed (a new `ddflow review`), the message "they stay on the record" is false: the handler keeps the prior `chunk_findings` only when the new evidence has no own findings (`evidence.setdefault`), and a fresh review delivers its own findings (and per the handler's own comment carries `review_kind`, which disables the copy entirely), so the old untriaged round is overwritten by the very command that printed the note. A user who follows the note's advice (`ddflow review triage <id> --gate critic --finding N`) after the command returns is triaging the new round's `chunk_findings`, not the earlier round's findings the note pointed at.
